thread.title: Apple’s earnings provide fodder for bulls and bears

author: Emily Bary
title: Apple’s earnings provide fodder for bulls and bears
text:
Apple Inc. provided something for everyone with its second-quarter earnings report.
iPhone units once again fell short of consensus expectations, stoking bearish concerns, but the company’s services segment posted a huge beat , supporting the bullish argument that Apple is AAPL, +4.03% not a one-trick pony. (A generous buyback program also helped.)
Shares are up 4% in Wednesday morning trading, but analysts largely dug in their heels after the results came out. Several upbeat analysts incrementally hiked their price targets, while skeptics found continued reason to be doubtful.
Don’t miss: Apple earnings were saved by the company’s new MVP
“We believe Apple’s ecosystem approach including an install base of over 1.3 billion devices globally is leading to record services revenue, and we expect the higher-margin services revenue growth to continue outpacing total company growth,” wrote Canaccord Genuity analyst Michael Walkley, who rates the stock a buy and raised his price target to $208 from $200.
Walkley called the iPhone numbers “better than feared” and reiterated his optimism about iPhone performance going forward. “We anticipate new OLED screen iPhones will launch in September 2018 to help drive a continued strong upgrade cycle to higher margin and higher ASP iPhones,” he wrote.
RBC Capital Markets analyst Amit Daryanani pointed to the diversity in Apple’s revenue stream. “We think slowly but surely, Apple is morphing into more than just an iPhone story and is displaying ability to sustain revenue growth irrespective of iPhone trajectory,” he wrote. Daryanani maintained his outperform rating and $203 target.
Morgan Stanley’s Katy Huberty cheered Apple’s recurring-revenue stream . “Services growth acceleration headlined a better-than-expected quarter and guide. Even if smartphone replacement cycles continue to lengthen, we see Apple delivering 4% revenue and 16% EPS growth over the next three years with services the primary growth engine,” wrote Huberty, who kept her overweight rating and $200 price target intact.
See also: Apple stock buybacks spiked to a new high as shares suffered a correction
Other analysts argued that there are still too many unknowns coming out of the report. “Looking forward, Apple didn’t provide enough information to fully vindicate iPhone X nor indicate its failure, so we don’t think investor concerns about iPhone units or mix will likely be put to rest until 4Q sell-through data is available in the fall,” wrote Raymond James analyst Chris Caso, who has a market perform rating on the stock.
Mizuho’s Abhey Lamba wrote Wednesday that investors may be more moved by the company’s capital-return announcements than by the actual results. “We think buybacks are likely to be used to support the stock through near-term softness in fundamental performance during the lull between product cycles,” wrote Lamba, who rates the stock at neutral with a $175 price target. Apple announced that it would be spending $100 billion more on buybacks as it has nearly exhausted its prior authorization of $210 billion.
BMO Capital Markets analyst Tim Long, who has a market perform rating and $171 price target on shares, said he has a number of unanswered questions about the latest numbers. “We are troubled by the disconnect between a very weak supply chain and slightly-better-than-seasonal iPhone performance,” he wrote. “We see a similar disconnect in China, where growth was great but we think units declined 10% year over year.”
Apple’s China revenue grew 21% in the March quarter, and Chief Executive Tim Cook said there were a number of reasons why, including services growth, wearables performance, and iPhone sales.
“The iPhone obviously had to do extremely well to get a 21% number,” he told investors on the company’s earnings call.
Read more: The surprise in Apple earnings was big growth in China
Apple shares are up 19% over the past 12 months, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, -0.13% of which Apple is a component, has gained 15%.
